abstract.text:
Abstract—The continuation power ﬂow method (CPF) has been
extensively used for obtaining the static voltage stability limit of
power systems, which provides important guidance for the sta-
ble operation. However, the conventional CPF cannot account for
the dynamic characteristics of renewable power generation, thus
resulting in prominent errors for renewable power generation-
penetrated power systems. In this brief, we investigate the static
voltage stability assessment (SVSA) of power systems with high
penetration of renewable power generation (RPG) . An extended
Jacobian matrix is ﬁrstly established by considering the dynamic
characteristics of synchronous generators (SG) and renewable
power generation in constant AC voltage control mode (CVRPG).
Based on the extended Jacobian matrix, an extended CPF method
is proposed for SVSA of the power system and a reactive power
sensitivity index is proposed to indicate the voltage support
capability of nodes. Simulation results show that the proposed
extended CPF method has higher accuracy than conventional
CPF in assessing the static voltage stability of power systems
with high penetration of RPG. It is also revealed that the voltage
support capability of each node rises as the proportion coefﬁcient
is increases.

introduction.text:
I. I NTRODUCTION
S
TATIC voltage stability characterizes the ability of a
power system to retain stable voltages under small dis-
turbances [1], [2]. Assessing the static voltage stability is
crucially important for power system operation. Recently, the
increasing integration of renewable power generation (RPG)
brings great challenges to the static voltage stability assess-
ment (SVSA), due to the distinct dynamic characteristics of
RPG compared with conventional power plants.
A set of previous studies investigated the inﬂuence of
RPG on the power system’s static voltage stability. A voltage

stability margin index was proposed to reveal the relation-
ship between control parameters and the stability margin in
real-time [3]. This index can reﬂect the inﬂuence of different
penetration levels of RPG on the static voltage stability limit of
the power system but with lower accuracy. The critical short-
circuit ratio were proposed in the literature to assess the static
voltage stability of the power system with integration of high
voltage direct current transmission (HVDC) [4], [5], [6], [7].
A modiﬁed short-circuit ratio was further proposed [8] by tak-
ing into account the impact of RPG. However, due to the
need for simultaneous solution based on detailed model, it
is too complicated to be applied to large-scale power systems.
Nodal voltage sensitivity that measures the weakness of a node
was adapted in [9] to study the impact of RPG on the power
system’s voltage stability. But the RPG nodes are treated as
constant power sources without considering their ability to
regulate the AC voltage. Data-driven methods based on AI
techniques were proposed in [10], [11], which have the poten-
tial for fast SVSA of power systems containing large-scale
RPG. But they require a large amount of online data and
the reliability of the results cannot be secured. Time-domain
simulations were used in [12] for assessing the static voltage
stability of power systems penetrated by RPG. This method
ensures high accuracy of the analysis results, but takes huge
computational costs.
The continuation power ﬂow method (CPF) has also been
most commonly used for SVSA of power systems, due to its
high analysis accuracy and applicability to large-scale power
systems. CPF obtains a continuum of power ﬂow solutions
from the intial power to the static voltage stability limit power
of power systems, and the criterion of reaching the limit is
whether the minimum eigenvalue of Jacobian matrix is zero.
However, its applicability declines with the continuous integra-
tion of RPG. In the conventional CPF, synchronous generators
(SG) are generally assumed with a constant voltage. This
treatment introduces insigniﬁcant errors because SG has a
nearly constant internal electromotive force (EMF) and rel-
atively small transient reactance. But when applied to RPG,
this treatment poses prominent errors due to the absence of
constant internal EMF [13], [14], [15].
In order to achieve fast and accurate SVSA for power
systems with high penetration of RPG, it is necessary to
improve the conventional CPF method by considering the
dynamic characteristics of RPG. In addition, a voltage support

ability index of nodes applicable to RPG is also conducive
to the rapid SVSA, due to that the reactive power sensitiv-
ity can reﬂect the static voltage stability level [16].T h em a i n
contributions of this brief are summarized as follows:
1) An extended Jacobian matrix is established that considers
the dynamic characteristics of SG and CVRPG;
2) An extended CPF method based on the extended Jacobian
matrix was proposed to realize the accurate SVSA of
power systems with high penetration of RPG ;
3) A reactive power sensitivity index is proposed to indi-
cate the capability of nodes in supporting static voltage
stability of the power system.
The rest of this brief is organized as follows: In Section II,
the power ﬂow model is introduced where the extended
Jacobian matrix is established by considering the dynamics
of SG and CVRPG nodes. In Section III, the extended CPF
method is proposed for SVSA of power systems with high
penetration of RPG and reactive power sensitivity index is
proposed to measure the voltage support capability of nodes.
In Section IV, simulations are performed to verify the accuracy
of the proposed SVSA method and to examine the inﬂuence
of control parameters.

conclusion.text:
V. C ONCLUSION
In this brief, we propose an extended CPF method for
SVSA of RPG-penetrated power systems, where an extended
Jacobian matrix is established by considering the dynamics of
SG and CVRPG nodes. Simulation results demonstrate that
the proposed method has higher accuracy than conventional
CPF and that the control parameters of CVRPG affect on the
voltage stability of the system.
Furthermore, the reactive power sensitivity index is
proposed to indicate the voltage support capability of nodes.
The work can be used for ﬁguring out the good operation con-
ditions of power systems and optimizing control parameters of
CVRPG, and will be further studied in our future work.
